sources.title: Sceau-cylindre : naissance de l'enfant divin
sources.author: Musee du Louvre, collection catalogue
sources.date: Catalogue: 2340-2200 BCE, Akkadian; Possehl gives later stylistic possibilities
sources.observation: Catalogue identifies Shilishu as interpreter of Meluhha. Discovery place is attributed by style, not a documented excavation locus.

sources.title: Shu-ilishu's Cylinder Seal
sources.author: Gregory L. Possehl
sources.observation: Reports checking the interpreter reading and explains the unprovenanced collection history. Late Akkadian/possible Ur III stylistic alternatives are retained rather than merged into the Louvre's date.

sources.title: The Middle Asian Interaction Sphere
sources.author: Gregory L. Possehl
sources.region: Mesopotamia, Gulf, Iranian plateau and Central Asia
sources.script_language: Discusses readable cuneiform records alongside imported objects
sources.observation: Identifies textual references to Dilmun, Magan, Meluhha, seafaring commerce and Meluhhan communities; separately identifies Indus-style objects abroad.
sources.limitation: A research synthesis and bibliography route, not an object-by-object edition or a count of fresh discoveries.

sources.title: BDTNS 157897
sources.author: BDTNS editors; edition K. De Graef 2005, MDP 54 p.150 no.29
sources.script_language: Catalogue language Akkadian; cuneiform tablet with seal legend
sources.date: Ur III period; exact tablet date not given
sources.observation: The record preserves a tablet and seal text with royal and official names/titles, including Shu-Suen and a governor of Susa.
sources.limitation: Several signs in the tablet are damaged or uncertain. No independent new translation or physical identity adjudication was performed.

sources.title: Stamped Tokens with Cuneiform Inscriptions from Bahrain: New Light on Kingship and the Gods in Early 2nd Millennium BC Dilmun
sources.access: institutional author abstract read; full article not inspected
sources.observation: The abstract reports three tokens bearing impressions of two seals naming Yagli-el and a divine servant epithet. It leaves the owner's identity with the namesake king as a research question.
sources.limitation: The deposited PDF is embargoed until 2027-04-01. No full plates, object accessions or linguistic classification were inferred from the abstract.

sources.title: Persepolis Fortification Tablets
sources.author: Richard T. Hallock
sources.access: institutional publication page read; no new PDF acquired
sources.script_language: Elamite cuneiform; archive also includes other languages
sources.date: Around 500 BCE; institutional overview gives the period down to 493 BCE
sources.observation: The publication provides edited administrative texts for food movements, allocations and sealed transactions. It is a later functional comparison, not contemporary Meluhha testimony.
sources.rights_notice: Publication landing page displays CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; captured source text remains local.

sources.title: Tamil - Brahmi Script
sources.author: Department of Archaeology, Government of Tamil Nadu
sources.access: indexed official page excerpt; direct web opens timed out
sources.region: South India, with overseas finds noted in Egypt and Thailand
sources.script_language: Tamil-Brahmi; individual texts require language adjudication
sources.date: Official overview: third century BCE to third century CE
identifiers: Karur silver ring bearing Peravatan; accession not supplied in the excerpt
sources.observation: The official overview lists cave inscriptions, pottery, coins, seals and rings, and reproduces a personal name on the Karur ring.
sources.limitation: No complete catalogue, image pixels or new record admission. Readable Tamil-Brahmi is kept separate from unclassified or undeciphered graffiti.

sources.title: Indians in Roman Berenike
sources.author: Sidebotham et al.; complete author list not transcribed in this scoping pass
sources.access: primary publication's indexed abstract/excerpts; direct page and viewer timed out
sources.region: Berenike and Myos Hormos, Egypt; comparative Sumhuram/Khor Rori, Oman
sources.script_language: Published Tamil-Brahmi pottery inscriptions; article also discusses other inscriptions
sources.date: Roman-period comparisons, including first-century CE material
sources.observation: Indexed passages describe fragmentary jar inscriptions from the Egyptian Red Sea ports and distinguish two claimed Sumhuram examples, one of which is regarded as uncertain.
sources.limitation: Full article and plates were not inspected. Specific reconstructed readings and disputed sherds are not admitted to a comparison corpus.
